items.bold: TRUMP CALLED OFF SCHEDULED IRAN ATTACK — "Serious negotiations taking place." Strike was planned for Tuesday.
items.text: CBS News live (3 hours ago) confirmed: President Trump posted on social media that he's not going ahead with a planned attack of Iran on Tuesday, saying serious negotiations are taking place. This is the single most important diplomatic development of the 80-day war. It confirms: (1) a strike was actively planned and scheduled for Tuesday May 19, (2) Trump chose to pause it — meaning Iran has made some movement toward talks, (3) the military option remains live but is not being executed today. The context: Trump emergency NSC meeting Sunday (Vance, Rubio, Ratcliffe, Witkoff) + "FAST or nothing left of them" post + UAE nuclear plant drone attack = strike was imminent. The calling-off is the biggest positive diplomatic signal since the ceasefire on April 8.

items.bold: KPLER DATA: 55 VESSELS crossed Hormuz May 11-17 — up from 19 previous week. Traffic returning to "average since conflict began."
items.text: CBS News live (3 hours ago) confirmed: traffic through the Strait of Hormuz was slightly higher last week, returning to levels in line with the average recorded since the start of the conflict, after hitting a wartime low. A total of 55 commodities vessels crossed the strategic waterway between May 11 and 17, according to data from maritime tracking firm Kpler as of Monday morning. The previous week, just 19 vessels crossed — the lowest weekly figure since the first US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. 55 vessels vs 19 = nearly 3x improvement week-on-week. Still far below pre-war 130-160 ships per day, but the directional signal is significant. The IRGC 30-vessel claim appears to have been partially real — Kpler data confirms genuine improvement in Hormuz transit volume. For India: India must urgently verify if any Indian-flagged vessels are among the 55 and submit PGSA applications immediately for LPG and fertiliser carriers.

items.bold: BRENT: $112 overnight high → below $107 Monday morning. Volatile but retreating on deal hope.
items.text: CBS News live (3 hours ago) confirmed: the price for a barrel of Brent crude oil went from a high of $112 overnight to below $107 in the morning before turning back higher. This extraordinary intraday move — $112 to $107, a $5 swing — reflects the market pricing the strike cancellation news in real time. $112 overnight = market pricing imminent US military strike on Iran. $107 by morning = market pricing strike called off + 55 vessels crossing + negotiations. The subsequent turn back higher = market uncertain whether negotiations will succeed. For India: Brent retreating from $112 toward $107-109 = partial OMC relief. At $107: OMC losses approximately Rs 16/L petrol, Rs 35/L diesel. If Brent falls further toward $100 on deal progress: OMC losses ease materially. Rupee may recover from 96+ ATL toward 95.50-95.80 on positive deal signal.

items.bold: IRAN: focused "entirely on agreement" — but HAS NOT DISCUSSED NUCLEAR matters. Gap remains on Trump admin's top issue.
items.text: CBS News live (3 hours ago) confirmed: Iran said it's focused entirely on an agreement to end the war, but has not discussed any details on nuclear matters — the Trump administration's top issue. This is the critical gap: Iran is willing to discuss an end to the war, Hormuz reopening, and ceasefire formalisation — but refuses to engage on nuclear. Trump called off the strike because negotiations are "serious" — but "serious" talks that avoid the nuclear issue cannot produce a comprehensive deal. Iran-Oman: Iran is in talks with fellow Strait of Hormuz coastal nation Oman "to develop a mechanism" to ensure "transit through the Strait of Hormuz." An Iran-Oman joint transit mechanism would give Iran's Hormuz control architecture Omani co-legitimacy — different from the pure IRGC toll system. This may be Iran's counter-proposal to a full deal: managed Hormuz opening without nuclear concessions.

items.bold: BESSENT general license: stabilize crude, reroute to energy-vulnerable countries, reduce China stockpiling discounted Iranian oil.
items.text: CBS News live (3 hours ago) confirmed: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced a new general license — "This general license will help stabilize the physical crude market and ensure oil reaches the most energy-vulnerable countries. It will also help reroute existing supply to countries most in need by reducing China's ability to stockpile discounted oil." This is a significant new US policy tool: allowing certain oil flows to "energy-vulnerable countries" (India, South Korea, Japan, Bangladesh) while limiting China's ability to arbitrage discounted Iranian crude. For India specifically: if the general license includes Indian refiners purchasing oil that would otherwise be stuck in the Gulf — this could provide partial crude import relief without a full Hormuz reopening. The "energy-vulnerable countries" language is directly aimed at India's situation. MEA must immediately engage Treasury on whether India qualifies for specific license exceptions under this general license.

assessment.body:
Tuesday 7:00 AM IST. Day 81. The most dramatic overnight of the 81-day war.

WHAT TRUMP DID
Called off a planned US military strike on Iran scheduled for Tuesday.
Posted: "Not going ahead with planned attack on Tuesday — serious negotiations taking place."
Context: Emergency NSC Sunday → "FAST or nothing left" → UAE nuclear plant attack → strike planned.
Calling it off means: Iran has made enough diplomatic movement to pause the military clock.
The military option is preserved: "full assault on a moment's notice if no deal."

WHAT KPLER CONFIRMED
55 commodities vessels crossed Hormuz May 11-17.
Previous week: 19 vessels — lowest since February 28.
Almost 3x improvement week-on-week.
Traffic returning to "levels in line with average since start of conflict."
The IRGC PGSA system is processing vessels at scale.
~8 vessels/day — still 95% below pre-war but genuine and measurable improvement.

WHAT BRENT DID
$112 overnight (strike priced in) → $107 Monday morning (strike cancelled) → turns back higher.
A $5 swing in hours — the fastest Brent move of the war.
Markets pricing: deal possible but not certain.
At $107-108: Brent still elevated but retreat from $112 = partial relief.

WHAT IRAN SAID AND DIDN'T SAY
"Focused entirely on agreement to end war." ✓
"Has not discussed nuclear matters." ✗ (Trump admin's top issue)
Iran-Oman transit mechanism talks. ✓ (managed Hormuz, Omani legitimacy)
The nuclear gap is the single remaining obstacle to a comprehensive deal.

WHAT BESSENT'S LICENSE MEANS FOR INDIA
"Energy-vulnerable countries" = India specifically.
A general license allowing Indian refiners to access crude that would otherwise be blocked by US sanctions.
MEA/Finance Ministry must engage Treasury TODAY for specific license exceptions.
This is partial crude import relief without requiring full Hormuz reopening.

INDIA'S TUESDAY MORNING
Gap-up expected 9:15 AM IST: Sensex +400-700, Nifty 23,600-24,000.
Rupee recovery from 96+ toward 95.50-95.80.
Kharif fertiliser: 55 vessels/week = Gulf sourcing viable — ORDER TODAY.
PGSA applications: submit for Indian LPG/fertiliser carriers.
Bessent license: engage Treasury.
Iran-Oman mechanism: engage via India's Oman relationship.

VERDICT: Day 81 is the morning after the most significant overnight of the war. Trump called off a strike that was planned for today. 55 vessels crossed Hormuz last week — nearly 3x the previous week. Iran and Oman are developing a transit mechanism. Bessent created a general license for energy-vulnerable countries. The war is not over — Iran has not discussed nuclear. But it is the closest to a managed de-escalation that Day 81 has seen. India must act on every one of these openings today: PGSA applications, Bessent license engagement, kharif fertiliser orders, Iran-Oman mechanism engagement through Oman. The window may be open for 48 hours. India cannot waste it.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
